questions.text: A projectile is launched at an angle ' $\alpha$ ' with the horizontal with a velocity $20 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. After 10 s, its inclination with horizontal is ' $\beta$ '. The value of $\tan \beta$ will be : $\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\right)$

options.D:
$2 \tan \alpha+5 \sec \alpha$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)

Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
v_{x}=u_{x}=20 \cos \alpha \\
v_{y}=20 \sin \alpha-10 \times 10 \\
\tan \beta=\frac{v_{y}}{v_{x}}=\frac{20 \sin \alpha-100}{20 \cos \alpha} \\
=\tan \alpha-5 \sec \alpha
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A girl standing on road holds her umbrella at 45° with the vertical to keep the rain away. If she starts running without umbrella with a speed of $15 \sqrt{2} k m h^{-1}$, the rain drops hit her head vertically. The speed of rain drops with respect to the moving girl is :

options.D:
$25 \mathrm{kmh}^{-1}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{V}=\tan \theta=\frac{V_{G}}{V_{R G}} \\
1=\frac{V_{G}}{V_{R G}} \Rightarrow 15 \sqrt{2}=V_{R G}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A sliver wire has mass $(0.6 \pm 0.006) \mathrm{g}$, radius $(0.5 \pm 0.005) \mathrm{mm}$ and length $(4 \pm 0.04) \mathrm{cm}$. The maximum percentage error in the measurement of its density will be :

options.D:
$7 \%$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
M=(0.6 \pm 0.006) \mathrm{g} \\
r=(0.5 \pm 0.005) \mathrm{mm} \\
l=(4 \pm 0.04) \mathrm{cm}
\end{array}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\rho=\frac{m}{V} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=\frac{\Delta m}{m}+\frac{2 \Delta r}{r}+\frac{\Delta l}{l}
\end{array}$$
(Volume of cylinder $=\pi r^{2} l$ )
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\frac{0.006}{0.6}+\frac{2 \times 0.005}{0.5}+\frac{0.04}{4} \\
100 \times \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=4 \times 10^{-2} \times 100 \\
\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100=4 \%
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A $72 \Omega$ galvanometer is shunted by a resistance of $8 \Omega$. The percentage of the total current which passes through the galvanometer is :

options.D:
$0.25 \%$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $S=\frac{R_{G}}{\frac{I}{I_{g}}-1}$
$$8=\frac{72}{\frac{I}{I_{g}}-1}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{I}{I_{g}}-1=9 \\
\frac{I}{I_{g}}=10 \Rightarrow \frac{I_{g}}{I}=\frac{1}{10} \quad \% I=\frac{I_{g}}{I} \times 100=10 \%
\end{array}$$

questions.text: What percentage of kinetic energy of a moving particle is transferred to a stationary particle when it strikes the stationary particle of 5 times its mass? (Assume the collision to be head-on elastic collision)

options.D:
$33.3 \%$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. Velocity after collision
$$\begin{array}{l}
V_{2}=\frac{\left(m_{2}-m_{1}\right) u_{2}+2 m_{1} u_{1}}{m_{1}+m_{2}} \\
V_{2}=\frac{(5 m-m) 0+2 m \cdot u_{0}}{m+5 m}=\frac{u_{0}}{3} \\
\% \Delta K E=\frac{\frac{1}{2} 5 m\left(\frac{u_{0}}{3}\right)^{2}-0}{\frac{1}{2} m u_{0}^{2}} \times 100 \\
=\frac{5 u_{0}^{2}}{9 u_{0}^{2}} \times 100=\frac{500}{9}=55.6 \%
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The velocity of a small ball of mass 'm' and density $\mathrm{d}_{1}$, when dropped in a container filled with glycerine, becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is $\mathrm{d}_{2}$, then the viscous force acting on the ball, will be :

options.D:
$m g\left(\frac{d_{2}}{d_{1}}-1\right)$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
$$F_{V}=m g-F_{B}$$

Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
=m g-\left(\frac{m}{d_{1}} \times d_{2}\right) g \\
=m g\left(1-\frac{d_{2}}{d_{1}}\right)
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The susceptibility of a paramagnetic material is 99. The permeability of the material in $\mathrm{Wb} / \mathrm{A}-\mathrm{m}$ is : [Permeability of free space $\mu_{0}=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~Wb} / A-\mathrm{m}$ ]

options.D:
$4 \pi \times 10^{-6}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol. Susceptibility $\chi=99$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mu_{r}=\frac{\mu}{\mu_{0}}=1+\chi \\
\mu=\mu_{0}(1+\chi) \\
=4 \pi \times 10^{-7}[1+99] \\
=4 \pi \times 10^{-5}
\end{array}$$

$2: \sqrt{3}$

questions.text: The displacement of simple harmonic oscillator after 3 seconds starting from its mean position is equal to half of its amplitude. The time period of harmonic motion is :

options.D:
36 s

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $X=A \sin \omega t\left(t=3, X=\frac{A}{2}\right)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \frac{A}{2}=A \sin 3 \omega \\
\Rightarrow \sin 3 \omega=\frac{1}{2} \\
\Rightarrow 3 \omega=\frac{\pi}{6} \\
\Rightarrow \omega=\frac{\pi}{18}=\frac{2 \pi}{T} \\
\Rightarrow T=36 \mathrm{~s}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: An observer moves towards a stationary source of sound with a velocity equal to one-fifth of the velocity of sound. The percentage change in the frequency will be :

options.D:
0\%

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $f_{0}=\left(\frac{v+v_{0}}{v}\right) f_{s}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
f_{0}=\left(\frac{v+\frac{v}{5}}{v}\right) f_{s} \\
f_{0}=\frac{6}{5} f_{s} \\
\% \text { change }=\frac{f_{0}-f_{s}}{f_{s}} \times 100 \\
=\frac{1}{5} \times 100=20 \%
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A hydrogen atom in is ground state absorbs 10.2 eV of energy. The angular momentum of electron of the hydrogen atom will increase by the value of : (Given, Plank's constant $=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$ )

options.D:
$4.2 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)

Sol. $13.6\left(\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{n^{2}}\right)=10.2$
$$\begin{array}{l}
n=2 \\
L_{i}=\frac{h}{2 \pi} \times 1 \\
L_{F}=\frac{2 h}{2 \pi} \\
\Delta L=L_{F}-L_{i}=\frac{h}{2 \pi}=\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{2 \times \frac{22}{7}} \\
=1.05 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J}-s
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen has volume $2000 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$, temperature 300 K, pressure 100 kPa and mass 0.76 g The ratio of number of moles of hydrogen to number of moles of oxygen in the mixture will be :

options.D:
$\frac{16}{1}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
n=\frac{100 \times 10^{3} \times 2000 \times 10^{-6}}{\frac{25}{3} \times 300} \\
n=80 \times 10^{-3} \\
n_{1}+n_{2}=0.08 \\
n_{1} \times 2+n_{2} \times 32=0.76 \\
\left(0.08-n_{2}\right) 2+n_{2}(32)=0.76 \\
n_{2}=0.02 \\
n_{1}=0.06 \\
\frac{n_{1}}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{1}
\end{array}$$
